scope: Real shared Coverage research tree; baseline plus three rounds, four proposals/select one per round; engineering verification, not surrogate efficacy

metadata.change_summary: Replace the RBF height surface with an inverse-distance-weighted contact surface whose heights are optimized from drillhole labels. Locally flat IDW surface at each hole makes signed distances close to vertical differences; heights optimized with the exact logistic + contact aggregate objective (analytic gradient). Local public-objective loss improves from 6.8774 to 6.5230, with 0 label mismatches and contact_rmse 0.2700.
metadata.rationale: Measured baseline was 405.0796 with 54 mismatches. The previous RBF surface got 6.8774 locally but suffered distance shrinkage from its dip and a fixed bias. The new solver extracts contact voxels, fits one height per drillhole under sign constraints, and optimizes those heights against the exact local logistic and global contact mean/variance terms. Using inverse-distance weighting gives zero surface gradient at each drillhole, so labels see nearly the maximum possible vertical distances. Public selfcheck passes; local copper.objective score is 6.5230 (research_utility -6.5230), close to the crossing-point lower bound of ~6.51 for this observation pattern. Contact-free fixtures use the RBF classifier fallback. Artifact: candidates/0/solver.py.

metadata.change_summary: Reworked the measured IDW contact-height solver into a 1-Lipschitz lower-bound solver: per-drillhole contact offsets are optimized against the exact vertical label bound plus the global contact mean/variance term, then realized with a super-Gaussian (p=3, sigma=3.75 cells) locally flat contact surface over an RBF base. Public local loss 6.51917 vs previous measured 6.52299.
metadata.rationale: Measured parent f3874... scored loss_total 6.52299 (0 mismatches, contact_rmse 0.27003). I derived a lower bound for any valid signed-distance field: with contact distance d, a label k cells away has distance at most k+d above and at least d-k below (1-Lipschitz), so its best logistic loss is fixed by d. Optimizing all contact offsets against this bound plus (mean d)^2 + mean(d^2) gives a proxy optimum of 6.51388 for this observation pattern, so no further large gain is possible from labels. The new solver computes these offsets from problem labels with L-BFGS-B, then uses locally flat super-Gaussian contact plateaus to approach the vertical distances while an RBF surface connects holes. Local copper.objective score is 6.51917, label_mismatches 0, contact_rmse 0.2707, public selfcheck passes. I tested Gaussian, p=2/3/4/6/8 weight shapes and sigma grids; p=3 sigma=3.75 was best. Fixed .275 offset scored 6.51957 locally, confirming the proxy offsets help slightly. Contact-free fixtures use the RBF fallback. This is algorithmic and consumes only the problem inputs.

metadata.change_summary: Replaced the super-Gaussian surface parameters and added exact contact-height correction. A broad r^4 locally-flat height blend (sigma=4.25 cells, small height bias) is now iteratively corrected so the blended surface passes through the optimized per-contact target heights. Local public-objective loss 6.51679 vs parent 6.51917, with 0 label mismatches and contact_rmse 0.27003.
metadata.rationale: Measured parent 591a... scored 6.51917 (0 mismatches, contact_rmse 0.27069). I retained its 1-Lipschitz offset optimisation, which is a rigorous lower-bound proxy (about 6.5139 for this pattern), and searched the surface realisation: nearest-contact plateaus were worse (6.555) because a high neighbouring plateau cuts distances above lower contacts; weighted nearest improved to 6.5236; a smooth r^4/height-biased blend reached 6.51682; and forcing the blended surface through each target contact height reduced it to 6.51679 while making contact_rmse exactly ~0.27003. The remaining 0.003 gap to the bound is from finite grid/skfmm distance realisations, not from a different contact-offset choice. Contact-free fixtures still use the RBF classifier fallback; public selfcheck passes. Artifact is candidates/0/solver.py (sha256 b7e7227e...).
